issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking only a permanent injunction is not maintainable without a declaration of title when the defendant raises a genuine dispute that creates a cloud over the plaintiff’s title.
material_facts: The plaintiff claimed to have purchased the property by registered sale deed and to have possessed it, including by constructing a residence.
The Board asserted that the property had been acquired and possession handed over to it, and relied on acquisition proceedings and a possession certificate.

The lower courts found that the plaintiff’s possession was proved and that the acquisition proceedings had not been shown to have attained finality, but granted an injunction without requiring a declaration of title.
The Supreme Court held that the Board’s reliance on the acquisition proceedings and possession certificate was sufficient to raise a cloud over the plaintiff’s title.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff should have sought a declaration of title, so the suit for a bare injunction could not be maintained; the decrees below were set aside. The parties were also directed to maintain the status quo as to possession temporarily.
issues.legal_principle: Under the settled principles stated in earlier judgments of the Court, a dispute about title does not in every case require the plaintiff to seek a declaration. A bare injunction suit is insufficient where the defendant raises a genuine title dispute that creates a cloud over the plaintiff’s title; in that circumstance, the plaintiff must seek a declaration. No particular provision or earlier case is identified by name in the judgment.

predicates.bare_injunction_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking an injunction to protect possession without seeking a declaration of title.
predicates.defendant_raised_genuine_title_cloud: The defendant relied on evidence or proceedings that genuinely put the plaintiff’s title in doubt.
predicates.declaration_not_sought: The plaintiff did not ask the court to declare the plaintiff’s title.
predicates.bare_injunction_suit_not_maintainable: The suit seeking only an injunction cannot be maintained without a declaration of title.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff brings only an injunction suit, the defendant genuinely puts the plaintiff’s title in doubt, and the plaintiff seeks no declaration, the suit cannot be maintained.

issues.legal_issue: A court must determine the nature of a suit from the pleadings and relief sought, and cannot treat a suit seeking only an injunction as a declaratory suit and adjudicate it on that mistaken basis.
material_facts: The plaintiff’s suit, as the Supreme Court read the pleadings and prayer, sought only a permanent injunction against interference with possession.
The lower courts treated the suit as one seeking a declaration of title, framed and decided title issues, and made findings about title, although the relief granted was an injunction.
The Supreme Court concluded that the lower courts had misconstrued the pleadings and confirmed their decisions without properly appreciating the factual and legal aspects.
issues.conclusion: The decrees below were set aside because the courts had misconstrued the suit as one for declaration when it sought only an injunction. The parties were also directed to maintain the status quo as to possession temporarily.
issues.legal_principle: The nature of the suit must be determined from its pleadings and the relief actually sought. A court must not proceed on the assumption that a suit seeks declaratory relief when the pleadings and prayer seek only an injunction. The judgment relies on the settled legal position but identifies no particular provision or earlier case by name.

predicates.appeal_from_lower_court_decree: A party appealed from a lower-court decree in a civil suit.
predicates.plaintiff_sought_only_injunction: The plaintiff’s pleadings and prayer sought only an injunction.
predicates.lower_courts_treated_suit_as_declaratory: The lower courts proceeded on the basis that the suit sought a declaration of title.
predicates.lower_courts_adjudicated_title: The lower courts framed or decided title issues and made findings about title.
predicates.challenged_decree_set_aside: The decree under appeal is set aside.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a decree in a suit whose plaintiff sought only an injunction, but the lower courts treated it as declaratory and adjudicated title, the challenged decree is set aside.
